articles.title: Broadridge Appoints Theo Golden as Head of Tokenized Product, International
articles.description: Broadridge, today announced the appointment of Theo Golden, CFA as Head of Tokenized Product, International, a newly created role. Golden will lead tokenized product development across Broadridge’s international markets, helping global clients adopt compliant, interoperable digital asset solutions at scale. “Tokenization is moving mainstream, and clients need infrastructure that can make tokenized products work compliantly at scale,” said Mark Nichols, Co-President, Digital Assets, Broadridge. “Theo combines deep experience in traditional finance with a proven ability to build first-of-its-kind tokenized products in a regulated environment. His client perspective and product expertise will be instrumental as we extend Broadridge’s digital asset leadership to international markets.” Golden will focus on designing, building and bringing to market tokenized products across capital markets, funds and tokenized assets. He will also support Corporate Development with mergers and acquisitions and strategic venture investment activity in digital assets. “I am excited to join Broadridge at a pivotal time for tokenization,” said Theo Golden, CFA, Head of Tokenized Product, International, Broadridge. “Global markets are moving quickly as frameworks for tokenized funds and securities evolve. Broadridge is exceptionally well positioned to deliver the trusted, resilient and interoperable infrastructure clients need to move from experimentation to real-world adoption. I look forward to helping build solutions that address tangible client needs and unlock the promise of global, 24/7 market rails.” Golden joins Broadridge from Baillie Gifford, where he served as Head of Digital Assets and built the firm’s digital asset capability from the ground up. He designed its digital asset strategy, operating model and key external relationships, and launched Baillie Gifford Enhanced Yield (BAGEY), the United Kingdom’s first fully native tokenized fund. Issued on Ethereum and Solana, BAGEY uses on-chain books and records as the legal source of truth while maintaining investor protections, governance and ownership rights. Prior to leading digital assets, Golden co-managed Baillie Gifford’s Strategic Bond Fund and worked as a multi-asset investment analyst. A CFA charterholder, he brings direct buy-side portfolio management experience and an understanding of the operational friction investors face across dealing, settlement, servicing and reporting. Earlier in his career, he worked in journalism at Business Insider, Bloomberg and Acuris. Golden’s appointment supports Broadridge’s next phase of digital asset innovation, extending its expertise beyond repo into funds, assets, capital markets and trading for clients worldwide. Based in London, he reports to Nichols and will work closely with Germán Soto Sanchez, Co-President and Chief Product Officer, Digital Assets; Horacio Barakat, Head of Digital Innovation; Seha Islam, General Manager for Digital Asset Platform and On-chain Governance; Mike Sleightholme, President, International and Asset Management; and teams across Broadridge’s platform pillars, business units and engineering organization. articles.title: Oskido Brings Durban’s Dance Music Legacy To Big Day Out
articles.sourceName: Brand Icon Image - Latest Brand, Tech And Business
articles.description: Durban’s Finest & Cndo Join Big Day Out In Celebration Of Ikhamanga, And FNB Announced As Official Partner GET YOUR TICKETS HERE Oskido’s Big Day Out is turning up the volume ahead of its third edition this November, announcing additional headliners to an impressive 2026 lineup alongside the formality of their partnership with FNB. DJ Tira and DJ Sox aka Durban’s Finest together with DJ Cndo have joined the 2026 lineup. Reinforcing Big Day Out’s commitment to showcasing the diversity of local music, this year’s festival will also celebrate Durban’s rich dance-music legacy and its defining influence on Mzansi’s music culture over the past three decades. From the influential Kwaito era to the sounds that continue to move audiences today, Durban has played a significant role in shaping the country’s dance-music landscape and has produced music that has resonated with and influenced generations. This year’s edition of Oskido’s Big Day Out will pay homage to this important chapter in South African music history, bringing together established pioneers, influential DJs and artists whose sounds continue to transcend generations. These Durban musical legends will add even greater energy, musical diversity and dancefloor appeal to the festival’s two-stage experience, creating a celebration of the sounds, artists and cultural moments that have helped shape Mzansi’s musical identity. Taking place on Saturday, 28 November 2026 at Huddle Park in Linksfield, Oskido’s Big Day Out will again bring together generations of music lovers for a full day celebrating the sounds, artists and cultural moments that have shaped SA music. This year’s Big Day Out is particularly special. Not only will we be celebrating Oskido’s birthday and also a significant milestone in his illustrious career with the Order of Ikhamanga, awarded to him by the presidency earlier this year in recognition of his outstanding contribution to South African music and culture. Adding another significant dimension to this year’s festival, one of South Africa’s most reputable financial institutions FNB, comes on board as an official partner of Oskido’s Big Day Out. The partnership brings together two brands with a shared focus on connection, experiences and enabling South Africans to do more with the moments that matter. With a longstanding commitment to supporting arts and culture, FNB continues to look beyond traditional banking by creating meaningful connections in the lifestyle spaces where its customers connect, express themselves and create memorable experiences. “Music has a unique ability to bring people together and create lasting memories. Oskido’s Big Day Out celebrates artists whose influence and success have endured for decades, reflecting the importance of longevity, relevance and the lasting impact of strong foundations, values that closely align with FNB’s commitment to helping customers build and preserve their own legacies. These same principles underpin our approach at FNB, where we believe trusted advice and long-term partnerships play a critical role in helping customers achieve their financial goals. This partnership allows us to connect with South Africans through authentic, culturally relevant experiences while helping them get more out of life and create meaningful moments with the people who matter most,” said Philani Potwana, CEO of FNB Private Core Banking and Credit Card. For Oskido, the partnership represents an exciting new chapter for a festival that continues to grow while remaining rooted in the music and culture that inspired it. “Big Day Out has always been about bringing people together through music,” says Oskido. “This year we are taking that experience even further. We have incredible artists from different eras, two stages and now a partnership with FNB that allows us to create even more opportunities for people to connect, celebrate and make memories together.” With several heavy hitters already confirmed, Big Day Out 2026 is shaping up as a celebration of where South African music has been, where it is now and where it is going next. And there is still more to come in the final phase of talent to be announced soon. So whether you are coming for the classics, the contemporary sounds, the energy of the dancefloor or simply to spend a day with friends and family, Oskido’s Big Day Out 2026 promises twice the music, twice the energy and a full day of unforgettable experiences. articles.title: ICC and CSA to unveil 2027 World Cup schedule on October 1- Report
articles.description: The ICC and CSA are expected to make the announcement about the schedule of the 2027 World Cup in Cape Town on Thursday, October 1, which will not only mark the commencement of the year-long countdown but will also be marked by the sale of tickets for the game. As reported earlier by Cricbuzz on August 15, the World Cup is supposed to begin on October 2, 2027—Gandhi Jayanti Day—and will end on November 21, 2027. The 2027 ICC World Cup will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. Ten of the 14 participating teams will have been confirmed for the World Cup by September 30, the cut-off date for qualification. Two of them will be the hosts, South Africa and Zimbabwe, while the other eight will make it on the basis of the ICC ODI rankings. The remaining four teams will be finalized through the qualifiers and will be listed in the schedule as Qualifier 1, 2, 3, and 4. Though Namibia is also a host country for the World Cup, they will have to play the qualifiers to play in the event. As of now, India (No. 1), New Zealand (No. 2), Pakistan (No. 4), Australia (No. 5), England (No. 6), Sri Lanka (No. 7), Afghanistan (No. 8) and Bangladesh (No. 9) are the eight teams in line to make the cut through the rankings. Bangladesh has pipped the West Indies to make it into the World Cup, as South Africa, the third-ranked team, is the host, and the West Indies will play the qualifiers, which are scheduled to be held early next year. The ICC will be starting the World Cup ticket ballot from Thursday. Though you won’t be able to buy any tickets right away, you can apply for your name to be included in the ticket ballot from October 1. According to an ICC press statement, the 2027 World Cup will have three preliminary stages prior to the semi-finals and final. The tournament begins with a Super Series, where the three lowest-ranked sides amongst the 14 sides that made the cut battle out in a round-robin series. The side that emerges on top moves to the next level. Round 2 consists of 30 matches, with 12 sides taking part, and they are divided into two groups of six who play in the round-robin series. The top three sides in each group, along with the best-performing side amongst the two groups, move on to the Super 7 round. The Super 7 series has 21 matches lined up in the round-robin stage, with the top four sides moving on to the semi-finals. During the semi-final stage, the side on top of the Super 7 series faces the fourth-place side, whereas the second side battles the third-place side. The winners from these two semi-final matches move forward to the finals. (Cricbuzz inputs)
